messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: seeds & random number streams
parts:
Hi!
 
Just a quick question concerning seeds (the manual was not too precise on that): In case I want to start multiple chains in parallel for my stan model, then I would do this:
 
./model init=0 seed=1234 id=1
./model init=0 seed=1234 id=2
 
Now all chains would start from the very same initial value *and* seed. However, does Stan use the id in order to make the random number generator streams independent? This is what I assumed all the time, but I was looking for a statement like this in the manual and could not find it.
 
Many thanks for clarification!
 
Best,
Sebastian

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] seeds & random number streams
parts:
Yes, the seed gets advanced by the chain id so those two chains would
indeed produce independent chains.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] seeds & random number streams

What does that mean? Is the "true" seed something like seed + id. I mean how does stan create independent random number streams from a seed and an id? I know how this work for L'ecuyer (or however it is spelled), but what is the stan way to do that?
 
This could be a bit more explicit in the manual (or I overlooked), but from quick going trough it, I only found that the id is a magic process id.
